text: Debugging can be frustrating, but a systematic approach makes it much easier. Start by identifying the bug clearly: what should happen, and what actually happens? Reproduce the problem first, as this gives you a starting point. Then, use debugging tools like breakpoints or step-through execution to inspect your code line by line. These tools let you see variable values and spot where things go wrong. Logging is another powerful strategy; adding print statements or log messages helps you trace the flow and observe data changes over time. Finally, test one hypothesis at a time, and don’t rush—patience often reveals the simplest solution.
